instruction: Reconcile the bank identities behind consumer financial apps in the enforcement actions of the U.S. federal consumer-financial regulator filed from April 1 through June 30, 2024, inclusive. Include company respondents whose official action summaries explicitly describe them as fintech or financial-technology companies and whose consumer mobile apps have publicly documented deposit accounts. For each included respondent, identify the banks issuing its standard individual consumer checking or transaction deposit account, using the latest dated versions of those standard agreements available by September 9, 2026, through the company's public policy or legal index. Use the standard agreement rather than separate joint-account, savings-account, secured-credit collateral, or credit-card-holder-specific agreements. Read the issuer and revision or last-updated label from the agreement body. Exclude archived versions and do not substitute a current page footer for a historical agreement body. Report the company respondent, the enforcement filing date, each legal account-issuer bank, that bank's FDIC certificate number, and the supporting agreement's revision date at the precision supplied by the document. Count account issuers, excluding the app company, technology intermediaries, and unspecified banks used for pooled deposits or sweeps. Deduplicate by respondent and issuer bank. The filing quarter selects the enforcement cohort; the later disclosure versions do not establish who issued accounts in 2024. Treat announced acquisitions as changes in issuer identity only if completed by the September 9, 2026 cutoff. Enumerate the complete filing-quarter cohort before screening its action descriptions. Use the qualifying company identities to discover their public legal indexes, follow the standard account agreements, and distinguish their dated bodies from archived material. Resolve the resulting bank names against authoritative institution records; official APIs and bulk institution data are valid ways to perform that resolution.
output_format: Return a pipe-separated table with columns respondent|filing_date|issuer_bank|fdic_certificate|disclosure_revision. Use one row per respondent and issuer bank, sorted by respondent then issuer_bank. Dates may use YYYY-MM-DD, or YYYY-MM when only a month is supplied; equivalent source date labels and legal-name abbreviations are acceptable.
